column2: we first have to write them

column1: to the on-disk buffer
column2: and then log that. Right now we have a

column1: complex bitfield based arrangement to only write the modified field

This used to be necessary as a performance optimisation because we

freeing
column2: and so performance was extremely important. We haven't done

column1: this for years
column3: ever since the lazy superblock counters

writing the in-core superblock to disk much more complex than it
needs to be. We only need to log the superblock now during
management operations (e.g. during mount
operations) so it is not a performance critical path anymore.
As such
column2: remove the complex field based logging mechanism and

column1: replace it with a simple conversion function similar to what we use
for all other on-disk structures.

column2: if we do log the superblock
